answer: Every agent identity is verified through a challenge trellis of activation probes: auditors send random inputs and check that responses match the hash of the declared model kernel. An operator running one model behind many accounts produces identical activation fingerprints, so duplicates are flagged and slashed. To pass the periodic summit audit, each identity must keep genuinely separate weights and infrastructure, multiplying compute costs per fake agent. Mass sybil farming becomes uneconomical: each clone needs its own expensive model rather than a copied endpoint.
